newsitem.title: FRANCE: Zaire's Mobutu delay return home.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Mobutu delay return home.

text.p: Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko has decided to delay his return home for a few days to pursue from France his search for a solution to the crisis in his central African nation, an aide said on Sunday.
The delay in returning to Zaire is unrelated to Mobutu's health, the aide added. Mobutu's entourage had earlier said he would return to Zaire at the weekend.

Mobutu, who is facing a rebel uprising in eastern Zaire in which his troops have fared poorly, left Zaire on February 21 for southern France, where he owns a luxury Riviera villa. He visited his doctors at a hospital in nearby Monaco the next day.

Mobutu underwent radiation therapy following prostate cancer surgery in Switzerland in August, his son and spokesman Mobutu Nzanga told Reuters last week, raising speculation that his regular visits to the Monaco hospital were for follow-up cancer treatments.
But Nzanga insisted the visits were for routine tests.

The aide said Mobutu had now decided to extend his stay in France until at least midweek so as "not to interrupt the work undertaken since his arrival in France, where it is easier to carry on consultations".

"His concern is to clarify the situation in the east. There are no negotiations under way with anyone, but there are discussions with the Americans and the Europeans, which has led to an impressive telephone ballet," the aide told Reuters.
South African President Nelson Mandela has launched a diplomatic initiative in hopes of achieving a cessation of hostilities and bringing the warring factions together for negotiations.
But Mobutu has repeatedly said negotiations cannot begin until all foreign troops have left Zaire.
Kinshasa accuses Rwanda, Burundi and Uganda of giving the rebels military support though Zaire's three eastern neighbours have denied involvement in the war, which began last October.

The war has triggered a grave humanitarian crisis in the Great Lakes region, where hundreds of thousands of mostly Hutu refugees have been stranded by the hostilities without adequate food supplies or medical care.

A rebel spokesman said on Sunday that rebel troops had captured the strategic town of Lubutu and the nearby refugee camp at Tingi Tingi, and were continuing their advance on Kisangani, Zaire's third largest city.
There was no independent confirmation of the advance and no word on the fate of the refugees.
